//: Senses (15 §4) an ordinary person has. A full-grown person standing in daylight is seen at once out to about 50 m and, in deep shadow, not beyond a step or two.
doc: Sight: sixty metres, two hundred degrees about the facing. Nothing is seen asleep, unconscious or dead (D-930).

//: Asleep, only a sound twenty times as loud at the ear is heard, and whatever is heard wakes the sleeper (`rules/sleep.json`): a footstep in the open within about three metres, a crouched one only from the next cell.
doc: Hearing: forty metres all round; asleep, only what is loud at the ear. Nothing is heard unconscious or dead (D-930).

//: Touch: feeling what lands on one's own body. It reaches no further than half a metre, one's own place, so a blow is felt only by whoever it lands on; and since nothing gives off touch standing still it finds nothing by sweeping, and sweeps once an hour. A sleeper feels a blow; the unconscious and the dead feel nothing (D-930).
doc: Touch: what lands on one's own body is felt. Nothing is felt unconscious or dead.
